Colours, light and visibility

Both rulebooks ask the same thing: a target's colour must stand out clearly against the background. Two-colour targets are not recommended. So colour is not a type of target. The course setter (the person who places the traps and sets the flight paths) picks a colour for each flight path so that you can see the target.

You will hear black, orange, white, yellow and pink targets. Many course setters use black against the sky and orange against trees and grass. A 'blazed' target has a bright orange painted dome. Careful: when a coach says 'the orange one', he means a colour, not a size. A black midi and an orange standard can come from the same stand.

If a target of the wrong colour is thrown, the referee calls No Bird and it is thrown again. In both disciplines shooting may be stopped for a sudden heavy downpour or a violent storm that looks short. In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ the referee decides this, in Compak® Sporting the Head Referee; if the stop may last long, the jury is told. The Compak® Sporting rules add that bad weather itself is not a reason for a No Bird: a hit counts and a miss is a miss, whatever the weather.

Light changes everything. Coaches talk about backlight (the sun behind the target), flat light on grey days, shadows under trees and the background behind the target: sky, tree line or ground. A target can 'disappear' against dark trees and 'pop out' against the sky. This is why shooters change the lens colour of their shooting glasses during the day.

Tip: On a new ground, many shooters try two lens tints on the first stand and keep the one that shows the target most clearly. See Shooting glasses and lens colours.

Key points

  • A target's colour must stand out against the background; two-colour targets are not recommended.
  • Colour is not type: 'the orange one' is a colour, not a size.
  • Wrong colour = No Bird.
  • Both disciplines: shooting may be paused for a short, violent storm. Compak® Sporting: bad weather itself is not a reason for a No Bird.
  • Backlight, flat light and the background change how a target looks.
Stand Talk

  • Coach The black one is the midi, the orange one is the standard — don't mix them up.

    Meaning: Two targets on the stand differ in colour and size.

  • Coach You lose it against the trees — pick it up later, in the sky.

    Meaning: The target is hard to see in front of trees; start watching where the sky is behind it.

  • Coach Flat light today — put the yellow lens in.

    Meaning: Grey light with little contrast; a yellow lens makes the target stand out more.

For the interpreter
  • When you translate, keep colour words and light words exact and short: 'it's coming out of the dark trees', 'you lose it in the sun'. They explain why a shooter missed, so they matter.

  • No Bird

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. What do the rules require of a target's colour?

    1. It must always be orange or white
    2. It must stand out against the background
    3. It must be two colours for contrast
    4. Any colour: the rules say nothing
    Answer

    It must stand out against the background

    Visibility against the background is the requirement; two-colour targets are not recommended.

  2. In Compak® Sporting it starts to rain hard and a shooter misses. Can he ask for a No Bird because of the weather?

    1. Yes, weather always justifies one
    2. Only for the first target of a double
    3. Only if the jury agrees to it
    4. No, weather is not a reason for a No Bird
    Answer

    No, weather is not a reason for a No Bird

    The Compak® Sporting rules say bad weather is not a reason for a No Bird: the miss stays a miss. Separately, the Head Referee may stop the shoot for a sudden storm that looks short.

    Chapter 20 · No NO BIRD for bad weather

  3. A coach says 'Watch the orange one.' What is he describing?

    1. The colour of a target
    2. A target size of 90 mm
    3. A rabbit
    4. A broken target
    Answer

    The colour of a target

    Colour is chosen for visibility and says nothing about size or type.
